abstracts.value: We present the first measurement of cosmic-ray fluxes of <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> isotopes in the rigidity range from 1.9 to 25 GV. The measurements are based on <math display="inline"><mrow><mn>9.7</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math display="inline"><mn>1.04</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></math> <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> nuclei collected by the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer on the International Space Station from May 2011 to October 2023. We observe that over the entire rigidity range the <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> fluxes exhibit nearly identical time variations and, above <math display="inline"><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>4</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>GV</mi></mrow></math>, the time variations of <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>, <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>, He, Be, B, C, N, and O fluxes are identical. Above <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">∼</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>GV</mi></mrow></math>, we find an identical rigidity dependence of the <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> fluxes. This shows that they are both produced by collisions of heavier cosmic-ray nuclei with the interstellar medium and, in particular, excludes the existence of a sizable primary component in the <math display="inline"><mrow><mmultiscripts><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi>Li</mi></mrow><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> flux.
